notes: kb/Work PB706 (2026-09-22). --check 12.4.5.10.3 "The RECORD SEQUENTIAL phrase specifies that the file organization is record sequential" -> OK 3). RECORD SEQUENTIAL binds to FileOrganization.Sequential (one value for record sequential, never a fourth) and the golden round-trips two records through it. Editions 2023: the phrase is written out only from 2023 (COBOL0900 below, conformance:cases/12.4.5.10-ORGANIZATION/pb706-record-sequential-below-2023). retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#MapOrganization (kb/Work PB2356 extracted the FILE-CONTROL entry binding and the I-O-CONTROL paragraph out of DataBinder.cs and DataBinder.IoControl.cs into the FileControlBinder class (and the COLLATING SEQUENCE alphabet test into SpecialNamesBinder); each member is the same rule, moved with its body unchanged) EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED 2026-11-10: in force at 85 IN PART, the definition of the organization and not the written word RECORD, §1985:VII.2.6.3 GR2 'Sequential organization is a permanent logical file structure in which a record is identified by a predecessor-successor relationship established when the record is placed into the file' (a 1985 'ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL' file, or one with the clause omitted, is the 2023 record sequential file, §2023:12.4.5.10.3 GR6; the spelled-out RECORD stays 2023 syntax as the notes above say, and the 2002 and 2014 tokens are forced by the validator's no-gap rule and rest on no 2002 or 2014 text read).
